The engineering team has abandoned JAX and SGLang, rewriting the entire RL and inference stack in C/C++

posts.text:
Elon Musk just revealed something huge about Grok's new SI training and inference infrastructure

The engineering behind Starlink is now helping power the development of Grok

SpaceXSI has completely rewritten Grok's reinforcement learning and inference software from scratch, replacing JAX and SGLang with its own system built primarily in C, with a little C++

And the most important part is where this engineering expertise comes from

The new stack is built on the incredible work of the engineers who created Starlink's incredibly complex satellite network

Elon explained:

"At SpaceX, we write our own headers and calculate our own time (includes leap seconds). Not many people will know what this means, but those that do will appreciate it."

Here's why that's significant

SpaceX engineers build and control critical parts of their software themselves, even down to the code interfaces and precise time calculations needed for satellite operations

This gives them much tighter control over how their systems operate, reducing unnecessary software dependencies and allowing them to optimize performance and reliability

Now that same engineering philosophy is being applied to Grok

posts.text:
In February 2004 Elon Musk wrote the check that put Tesla Motors on the road: $6.5 million of a $7.5 million Series A, plus the chairman's seat.

He led the next round in February 2005. He co-led the $40 million round in May 2006 that brought in Larry Page and Sergey Brin. That August he published The Secret Tesla Motors Master Plan on the company blog, a sports car to pay for an affordable car, and so on down to the mass market. He pushed for the Roadster's carbon fiber body. By January 2009, Bloomberg reported, he had put $70 million of his own money into the company.

CNBC still wrote this on September 10, 2018: "Though Musk didn't found Tesla, his DNA is very much a part of the company."

Read the very next sentence of the same article: "He was one of its original investors and chairman of the board in 2004 before becoming CEO in 2008."

Original investor. Chairman in 2004. CNBC typed both facts and still filed him under "didn't found."

That question had been settled nine years earlier, in court and in writing. In 2009 Martin Eberhard sued, and one of the things he asked a San Mateo County judge for was a declaration that he and Marc Tarpenning were the only two founders. In July the judge struck that request. In September the case was settled and Tesla named five co-founders: Eberhard, Tarpenning, Elon Musk, JB Straubel and Ian Wright.

Eberhard's own statement that day: "As a co-founder of the company, Elon's contributions to Tesla have been extraordinary."

The man who went to court over the title called Elon Musk a co-founder in his own words. A business network still decided it knew better.

Elon Musk has told his side too. In April 2022 he wrote that the Tesla he walked into was "a shell corp" with "literally nothing but a biz plan to commercialize AC Propulsion's Tzero car, which was introduced to me by JB Straubel, *not* Eberhard." Then: "If filing a shell corp constitutes 'founding a company', then I'd be the only founder of PayPal, since I filed the original incorporation docs for http://X.com (later renamed PayPal), but that's not what founding means."

And the line that says the most: "I put in all I had, whereas Eberhard, who was worth over $10M at the time, refused to invest a penny to help Tesla."

So why slip a false founder line into a 2018 piece? Look at the headline it sat under: "Musk's defiant, rebel CEO persona is putting his company and its investors at risk, say management experts." The article argued Tesla needed "someone to help keep Musk in line." Shrink his role at the birth of the company and it gets much easier to argue he is replaceable at the top of it. Legacy media has been running that play on Elon Musk for years.

Tesla closed at $19.03 a share, split-adjusted, the day that story ran. On November 9, 2026 it closed at $378.05. The investors CNBC's experts were so worried about made nearly twenty times their money by keeping him exactly where he was.

JUST IN: Memphis Mayor reveals SpaceX data center taxes more than doubled to $54 million, after $25 million last year made it Shelby County’s second largest taxpayer

Paul Young was asked about Elon Musk’s claim that data centers have Memphis booming:

Q: “Recently, just speaking on the revenues the data centers are creating for Memphis. Elon Musk recently tweeted that Memphis is 'booming' because of the data centers. He said that hotels and restaurants are full and called, tax revenue in Memphis tremendous right now. Do you just have any thoughts on that?”

YOUNG: “Well, we’ve talked a lot about the financial aspects of the project. I think that as we talk about data centers in our city, we want to talk about it in a balanced way. Of course there’s an economic side. We want to make sure that we are articulating what protections and guardrails we’re putting in place for the environmental sides that, people are concerned about, the quality of life, noise, traffic, all of those aspects."

"But, there there is tax revenue. I think this year it was $54,000,000 in taxes that have been generated. And I know last year when they generated about $25,000,000 in tax revenue, it was the second largest tax paying property in Shelby County. I don’t know where $54,000,000 puts it, but it is significant taxes."

"And so as we look at, the tax revenue, we also wanna look at how do we ensure that there are proper protections. That’s what this ninety day executive order has been about, and, it’s the conversation that we’ll continue to have with the community.”

quote.author: firesidealpha
quote.name: Fireside Alpha
quote.text:
SpaceX’s Arizona data center, per a county supervisor: “We could be reducing property taxes across the board in Cochise County, the entire county, by 20%”

Frank Antenori, whose district includes the site, brought up the county’s tax math during a live Q&A:

“Here’s just something to just chew on. Arizona has an expenditure limit requirement that is placed on counties. If we exceed that expenditure, we have to rebate back to the taxpayers a certain amount.”

“So, if we’re receiving revenue in from SpaceX, by law, we have to offset that to the taxpayers. We have the potential to reduce, based on the projected revenue they’re creating, as much as 20%.”

“Let me just say it again. We could be reducing property taxes across the board in Cochise County, the entire county, by 20% to offset for the revenue here, because we can’t spend all that money. So, we have to give that money back to the taxpayers. The law says we have to.”

“So, you could see a potential significant impact to local property taxes. What that is, I don’t know. We’re going to have to do the math on it. But the law, if we have this large increase in property tax revenue, we have to balance those rates. So that will reduce dramatically the property tax burden of every resident in the county.”

“The construction sales tax, which also is the TPT, the transaction privilege tax, the retail tax, and the jail excise tax. So that will be part of the construction tax. We could literally use that money to pay the jail off in 2 to 3 years, as opposed to the 13 to 20 years.”

“So this could be a revenue to eliminate the half-cent sales tax in 2 to 3 years. We can get rid of that half-cent sales tax.”

Most people assume SpaceX began because Elon Musk wanted to build rockets, but the original idea was smaller. 

Around 2001 he looked for the date of NASA's Mars mission, discovered there were no plans to send people at all, and came up with Mars Oasis, a little greenhouse with seeds in dehydrated gel that would land on Mars and send back an image of green plants against red soil, just to get people excited about space again and help NASA get a bigger budget. 

Then he realized the real obstacle was the cost of rockets: "I was wrong… there actually was plenty of will if people thought there was a way. So then I decided, okay, well, I need to work on the way." 

SpaceX was born to serve the dream of exploration, not to compete with it 🩵
